# Check-in for Croatia: full reference

> Free, open-source, browser-only generator for the Croatian eVisitor
> `TouristCheckIns.xml` bulk-import file. https://checkin.villalavacroatia.com/

This file is the long version of https://checkin.villalavacroatia.com/llms.txt

## Who it is for

Anyone renting out accommodation in Croatia: a house, an apartment, a room, a
handful of units. Most people in that position run one or two properties and do
the paperwork themselves, usually on a Saturday in August with the next arrival
already in the driveway.

It is equally for their guests, who are the people actually holding the
passports the details come from.

## The obligation it helps with

Croatian law requires accommodation providers to register every overnight stay
with the authorities through eVisitor, within 24 hours of the guest's arrival.
eVisitor is also how the tourist tax (boravišna pristojba) is calculated. The
requirement itself is ordinary; most countries in the region track overnight
stays the same way.

Per guest, eVisitor wants: given name, family name, optionally a middle name,
sex as printed on the travel document, date of birth, citizenship, country and
city of birth, country and city of residence, travel document type and number,
arrival date and time, departure date and time, a tourist tax category, and an
arrival code from the Ministry of the Interior (MUP).

## Why the tool exists

The reasoning behind eVisitor is sound. The platform built on top of it is the
problem:

- The interface is half English and half Croatian, switching between the two
  inside a single screen and sometimes inside a single form. Neither a foreign
  owner nor a Croatian one gets a coherent interface, and the inconsistency
  means people learn it by position rather than by reading it.
- The session times out while you are squinting at a passport.
- It asks for the same property details for every guest, every time, despite
  already knowing them.
- There is no sensible way to hand the typing to the guest, who is the one
  person who can read their own document accurately.

The result is that passport details reach a host as a blurry photo in a
messaging app, or a name spelled three different ways across an email thread,
and then get retyped field by field. Every hop is a chance to introduce a wrong
passport number, which surfaces much later.

## How it works

### Guest mode

The guest opens the page, picks "I'm a guest", and fills in their own details
from their own document. They save a small XML file to their device and send it
to their host however they already talk to them. Nothing is uploaded by the
page.

### Host mode

The host saves property defaults once: facility code, travel agency OIB if
relevant, default MUP arrival code, and default check-in and check-out times.
These persist in that browser only.

For each stay the host either imports the file the guest sent or adds the guest
by hand, then fills the parts a guest cannot know: the tourist tax category and
the arrival code. The host saves one file containing every guest and uploads it
to eVisitor under **Turisti → Prijava putem datoteke**.

## The file it produces

A UTF-8 XML document with a `TouristCheckIns` root and one `TouristCheckIn`
element per guest. Element order follows eVisitor's schema, because the import
reads a positional contract. Dates are serialised in the compact `YYYYMMDD`
form, times as `HH:MM`, countries as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, and sex as `M`
or `F`. Empty optional fields are omitted rather than emitted blank.

Values are XML-escaped. Dates are validated against the real calendar, so a
date like 31 February is refused at the point of typing rather than silently
serialised for eVisitor to reject.

## Privacy

The page is static and makes no network requests at all: no server, no account,
no database, no analytics, no third-party scripts, no fonts or styles loaded
from anywhere else. Guest details live in `sessionStorage` and are gone when
the tab closes. A host's property defaults live in `localStorage` and can be
cleared from the page.

Sending the file to a host does travel over the internet, by email or a
messaging app or whatever the two people already use, exactly as a photo of the
passport would have. The difference is that no service in the middle keeps a
copy, no account is created, and nothing is logged. Compared with a passport
photo sitting in a chat thread indefinitely, that is the improvement on offer,
and it is the honest size of the claim.

## Limitations and caveats

- It never communicates with eVisitor. It produces a file; a human logs in and
  uploads it. Nothing is submitted on anyone's behalf.
- It is unofficial. Not affiliated with eVisitor, the Croatian National Tourist
  Board, the Ministry of the Interior, or any government body.
- The published Web-API wiki names every field but does not ship a sample
  document, and some lookup tables (tourist tax categories, MUP arrival codes)
  are not published at all, so a few values are best-effort. Check the first
  file you upload, and report anything eVisitor rejects.
- It does not replace a host's own record-keeping.

## Technical notes

Static single page. TypeScript compiled with Bun, Tailwind CSS v4, no runtime
framework. Fonts and styles are self-hosted. Colours are Catppuccin, Latte in
light mode and Mocha in dark. Deployed to GitHub Pages.

Licence: GNU AGPL v3 or later. The Affero clause is deliberate: anyone
deploying a modified copy for others to use over a network has to publish that
source, which is what lets a host verify the version they are typing into.
